metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with deployable entry points (index.cfm, download.cfm served by IIS/ColdFusion) and no IaC, container, or CI/CD artifacts.
metadata.archetype_justification: Both in-repo endpoints are read paths over a persistent SQL Server store (search/list with query-string filtering, plus file retrieval), with minimal business logic and no write endpoints or state mutations.

top_gaps.title: Monolith vs Microservices
top_gaps.gap: CFML pages mix presentation, authentication, and SQL with no module boundaries or data access layer.
top_gaps.impact: Blocks incremental modernization; triggers Move to Cloud Native and the Decomposition Strategy.

top_gaps.title: Managed Compute
top_gaps.gap: Single Windows EC2 instance running IIS 7 + ColdFusion 8; no container or serverless compute.
top_gaps.impact: Manual patching and capacity planning; triggers Move to Containers.

top_gaps.title: Managed Databases
top_gaps.gap: SQL Server 2005 self-managed, EOL since April 2016, no managed failover or backups.
top_gaps.impact: Operational burden plus unpatched data tier; triggers Move to Managed Databases.

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: Deployment is copying .cfm files over a network share into wwwroot.
top_gaps.impact: No reproducible release path or rollback; triggers Move to Modern DevOps.

top_gaps.title: Secrets Management
top_gaps.gap: Datasource password 'cfadmin' documented in plaintext in README.md.
top_gaps.impact: Version-controlled plaintext credential — deployment-blocking security issue.

findings.title: Managed Compute
findings.description: All compute runs on a single raw EC2 instance: README.md documents Adobe ColdFusion 8 on IIS 7, Windows Server 2008 (EOL) on a single Windows EC2 instance. No ECS/EKS/Lambda/Fargate definitions and no container images exist in the repository.
findings.gap: Zero managed-compute adoption; patching, capacity planning, and recovery are manual on an EOL OS and application server.
findings.recommendation: Re-platform the two read endpoints onto a supported runtime on ECS/Fargate (or Lambda behind API Gateway) and retire the Windows Server 2008 / ColdFusion 8 instance rather than re-hosting it.

findings.title: Managed Databases
findings.description: The backing store is self-managed SQL Server 2005 (README.md), reached via the ColdFusion datasource 'docportal' used by <cfquery> in index.cfm and download.cfm. No aws_rds_*, aws_dynamodb_*, or other managed-database resources exist.
findings.gap: A commercial, self-managed, end-of-support database with no managed failover, automated backup, or patch management.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for SQL Server (lift) or Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL (license reduction) via AWS DMS, enabling Multi-AZ, automated backups, and KMS encryption at cutover.

findings.title: Network Security
findings.description: No network definition exists in the repository — no VPC, subnet, security group, or network policy. README.md states the portal runs HTTP only on the internal network on a single instance, with no HTTPS and no segmentation between the web tier and the co-located database.
findings.gap: No custom VPC, no private subnets, no least-privilege security groups, no tier separation, and cleartext HTTP transport for authenticated sessions.
findings.recommendation: Define the target network in IaC: application tier in private subnets behind a load balancer, database in isolated subnets restricted to the app tier, TLS at the entry point, and VPC endpoints for AWS service access.

findings.title: API Entry Point
findings.description: The .cfm pages are served directly by IIS on the instance. No API Gateway, AppSync, ALB, or CloudFront definition exists, and no throttling, request validation, or gateway-level auth is configured.
findings.gap: Direct service exposure with no managed entry point, so there is no central place to enforce TLS, throttling, authentication, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Place Amazon API Gateway or an ALB in front of the re-platformed service with TLS, request validation, and throttling; add CloudFront if document delivery benefits from caching.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling
findings.description: No auto-scaling configuration exists. README.md describes a single instance with statically provisioned capacity; there is no Auto Scaling group, application auto-scaling, or scaling policy in the repository.
findings.gap: All capacity is static — traffic spikes degrade the single instance and idle periods waste reserved capacity.
findings.recommendation: After re-platforming, configure target-tracking auto-scaling on the service (ECS service auto-scaling or Lambda concurrency) and scale the data tier via RDS/Aurora capacity settings.

findings.title: Backup and Recovery
findings.description: No backup configuration exists for either data store. README.md states documents are on local disk with no object storage and no offsite backups, and that disk loss equals data loss. No aws_backup_plan, RDS retention setting, or snapshot lifecycle policy exists.
findings.gap: Neither the document corpus nor the database has an automated, retained, restorable backup, and there is no documented or tested restore procedure.
findings.recommendation: Move documents to S3 with versioning and lifecycle policies; enable automated backups with defined retention and PITR on the managed database; register both in AWS Backup and test a restore.

findings.title: High Availability and Fault Isolation
findings.description: The documented topology is a single EC2 instance hosting both web tier and database, with documents on its local disk: README.md states single instance, reboot equals downtime, disk loss equals data loss. No multi-AZ configuration or load balancer exists.
findings.gap: Single point of failure across compute, data, and storage with no automatic recovery from instance or AZ failure.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the re-platformed service across 2+ AZs behind a load balancer, run the database as Multi-AZ managed RDS/Aurora, and store documents in S3.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
findings.description: No IaC exists. A recursive scan found only README.md, index.cfm, download.cfm, and .gitignore — no .tf/.tfvars, CloudFormation, CDK, SAM, Helm, or Kustomize. The compute, network, database, and document-storage surfaces this app depends on are all unmanaged by code.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage (ClickOps) — infrastructure is non-reproducible and cannot be recreated for DR or for a non-production environment.
findings.recommendation: Define target-state infrastructure in CloudFormation or CDK before migration — network, compute, managed database, S3 document bucket, entry point, alarms, and backup plans.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation
findings.description: No pipeline definitions exist — no .github/workflows/, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, buildspec.yml, or appspec.yml. README.md documents the deployment method as copying .cfm files over the network share to wwwroot.
findings.gap: Fully manual deployment with no build, test, approval gate, artifact versioning, or rollback, for both application and infrastructure changes.
findings.recommendation: Build a CodePipeline/CodeBuild pipeline with build, automated test, and deploy stages plus automated rollback, and route infrastructure changes through the same pipeline via CloudFormation/CDK.

findings.title: Programming Languages
findings.description: The application is written entirely in CFML for Adobe ColdFusion 8 (index.cfm, download.cfm; README.md: built 2007 with Adobe ColdFusion 8). CFML on an unsupported ColdFusion 8 engine has effectively no cloud-native tooling ecosystem and no first-class AWS SDK support; there is no dependency manifest of any kind.
findings.gap: The runtime is unsupported with known critical CVEs, and the language choice requires custom integration for any AWS service adoption — modernization needs a runtime migration, not a framework upgrade.
findings.recommendation: Re-implement the two read endpoints in a mainstream cloud-native runtime with first-class AWS SDK support (Python 3.12, Node.js 20/TypeScript, Java 21, or .NET 8). If CFML must be retained, migrate to the maintained open-source Lucee engine on Linux as an interim step.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices
findings.description: A single deployable unit of page templates with no module boundaries. index.cfm combines <cfapplication> session configuration, authentication gating, HTML presentation, and an embedded SQL query against the shared documents table; download.cfm embeds its own query and builds a filesystem path inline. There is no package structure, interface layer, or data access layer.
findings.gap: Presentation, authentication, and persistence are interleaved per file with direct shared-table access from multiple entry points, blocking independent deployment, testing, and incremental replacement.
findings.recommendation: Follow the Strangler Fig approach: extract a document-search service and a document-retrieval service behind an Anti-corruption Layer over the existing documents schema, introducing a data access layer and removing inline SQL from templates.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling
findings.description: Archetype-calibrated for data-gateway. index.cfm issues SELECT ... FROM documents WHERE title LIKE '%#url.q#%' ORDER BY uploaded_on DESC with no row limit, no pagination, and a leading wildcard that forces a full scan, then renders every row synchronously. download.cfm streams a file of arbitrary size synchronously via <cfcontent>. No async job, status polling, or callback mechanism exists.
findings.gap: Heavy reads are synchronous and unbounded, so response time scales with table size and document size — the data-gateway 'heavy reads risk timeout' condition rather than a missing async-job platform.
findings.recommendation: Add server-side pagination and a row limit, replace the leading-wildcard LIKE with indexed full-text search, and serve documents via pre-signed S3 URLs so large-file transfer no longer occupies an application request.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy
findings.description: Endpoints are bare page names (index.cfm, download.cfm?id=) with no version segment, no version header handling, and no OpenAPI or changelog artifact. The 'v2.3' footer label in index.cfm is a product label, not an API version contract.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy, so any change to query parameters or response shape breaks all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Expose the re-platformed read paths under explicit versioned routes (e.g., /v1/documents, /v1/documents/{id}/content), publish an OpenAPI specification, and define a deprecation policy.

findings.title: Service Discovery
findings.description: All dependency locations are hard-coded: both pages reference the datasource by the literal name 'docportal' (resolved in CF Administrator, outside the repository), download.cfm hard-codes the storage root D:\docroot\files, and navigation targets are literal page paths. No service registry, mesh, or environment-based configuration is used.
findings.gap: Endpoints and storage locations are compiled into the application, so relocating the database or document store requires editing source files; there is no environment-specific configuration mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Externalize datasource and storage locations into configuration (environment variables backed by SSM Parameter Store / Secrets Manager) and use AWS Cloud Map or an ALB/API Gateway DNS name instead of literal paths.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage
findings.description: Documents are stored on local disk and served from it: download.cfm builds filepath = "D:\docroot\files\" & doc.filename and streams it with <cfcontent>. README.md confirms local file storage with no object storage and no offsite backups. No S3 bucket and no parsing/extraction pipeline (Textract, Tika) exists.
findings.gap: The document corpus — the portal's core asset — sits on one instance's disk with no durability, lifecycle management, server-side encryption, or text extraction, and makes the application non-stateless.
findings.recommendation: Migrate documents to Amazon S3 with versioning, SSE-KMS encryption, and lifecycle policies; serve via pre-signed URLs or CloudFront; add a Textract/Tika extraction pipeline to populate searchable text and metadata.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer
findings.description: Each page opens its own inline query against the docportal datasource: index.cfm embeds <cfquery name="docs"> inside its HTML and download.cfm embeds a separate <cfquery name="doc">. There is no repository, DAO, service layer, or ORM.
findings.gap: Data access is scattered with no shared pattern, duplicating query, parameter, and error handling — and it is the direct cause of the unparameterized SQL in both pages, since nothing enforces parameterization centrally.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a single data access layer (repository per aggregate) with parameterized queries only, and forbid direct SQL in presentation code.

findings.title: Database Engine Version and EOL
findings.description: README.md records the engine as SQL Server 2005 (EOL April 2016) and lists it as a known issue. No engine version is pinned anywhere, because no IaC or compose/Helm configuration exists in the repository.
findings.gap: The engine is more than nine years past end of support, receives no security patches, and its version is not managed declaratively — so there is no version-update, downtime, or rollback procedure.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a supported managed engine (RDS for SQL Server at a current major version, or Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL), pin the engine version in IaC, enable automatic minor version upgrades, and document the major-version upgrade procedure.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest
findings.description: A data-at-rest surface exists (SQL Server database plus the D:\docroot\files document volume) with no encryption configuration for either. No aws_kms_key, kms_key_id, or engine-level encryption setting appears in the repository; README.md describes plain local-disk storage.
findings.gap: Neither the document corpus nor the database has documented encryption at rest, and there is no key management or rotation policy.
findings.recommendation: Enable SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key on the S3 document bucket, enable storage encryption with a customer-managed KMS key on the managed database at migration, and document a rotation policy.

findings.title: API Authentication
findings.description: No token-based authentication exists. index.cfm gates on a server-side session (structKeyExists(session, "userid") then redirect to login.cfm), but download.cfm performs no authentication or authorization check at all — it accepts url.id, looks up a filename, and streams the file. README.md documents session fixation with no token rotation and HTTP-only transport, so the session cookie travels in cleartext.
findings.gap: The endpoint that returns actual document content is unauthenticated and directly addressable, and the authenticated endpoint relies on a non-rotating session over cleartext HTTP. No per-request token validation or per-document authorization exists.
findings.recommendation: Enforce authentication on every endpoint including document retrieval via OAuth2/JWT validated at API Gateway or in middleware; add per-document authorization checks; rotate session identifiers on login; require TLS.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration
findings.description: Authentication is entirely application-managed: index.cfm declares its own session scope via <cfapplication name="docportal" sessionmanagement="yes" ...> and reads session.userid / session.fullname set by a local login.cfm. README.md states auth is application-managed sessions with no SSO. No Cognito, OIDC, or SAML configuration exists.
findings.gap: A standalone identity silo with no external IdP federation, so access cannot be governed by central policy, MFA, or deprovisioning, and the app cannot participate in SSO.
findings.recommendation: Federate authentication to a centralized identity provider (Amazon Cognito user pools with SAML/OIDC to the corporate IdP), remove local credential/session handling, and derive authorization from IdP claims.

findings.title: Secrets Management
findings.description: A plaintext production credential is committed to the repository: README.md states the datasource credentials are configured in CF Administrator and the password is "cfadmin". The docportal datasource referenced by both pages is backed by that credential. No Secrets Manager, Vault, or Parameter Store usage exists.
findings.gap: A database password is exposed in version control (and is a trivially guessable default), with no secrets manager, encryption, or rotation — any repository reader obtains database access.
findings.recommendation: Treat the credential as compromised: rotate it immediately, remove it from documentation, and purge it from git history. Store the datasource credential in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation and retrieve it at runtime via an instance/task role.

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching
findings.description: No patching or vulnerability-scanning mechanism exists — no SSM patch baseline, Inspector/Snyk configuration, hardened base image reference, .github/dependabot.yml, or renovate.json. README.md documents Windows Server 2008 (EOL) and that ColdFusion 8 is unsupported with multiple critical CVEs.
findings.gap: An end-of-support OS and application server with known critical CVEs, no patch management, and no vulnerability scanning on a network-reachable host.
findings.recommendation: Treat the runtime as unremediable in place: re-platform onto a supported hardened base image (or serverless), then enroll compute in SSM Patch Manager, enable Amazon Inspector, and add dependency-update automation.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline
findings.description: There is no pipeline and therefore no security validation: no SAST configuration, no dependency scanning (npm audit, pip-audit, Dependabot, Renovate), no container scanning, and no .snyk policy. The repository contains no CI definition of any kind.
findings.gap: No automated detection of the vulnerabilities already present — the unparameterized SQL in both pages and the path-traversal exposure in download.cfm would be flagged by basic SAST, but nothing runs it.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI pipeline with SAST (Semgrep or CodeGuru Reviewer) and dependency scanning with a blocking gate on critical findings, plus ECR image scanning once containerized.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing
findings.description: No tracing instrumentation exists. Neither index.cfm nor download.cfm contains OpenTelemetry or X-Ray instrumentation, and no trace header (traceparent, X-Amzn-Trace-Id) is read or propagated. There is no dependency manifest through which a tracing SDK could be present.
findings.gap: Request flows — including the database call and the file-streaming path — are not traceable, so latency and failure diagnosis is guesswork.
findings.recommendation: Instrument the re-platformed service with OpenTelemetry or the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry, propagate trace context from the entry point, and send traces to AWS X-Ray.

findings.title: SLO Definitions
findings.description: No monitoring artifacts of any kind exist in the repository — no SLO definitions, no CloudWatch alarms in IaC (there is no IaC), no latency or error-rate thresholds, and no dashboards. The application has a user-facing surface for which SLOs would be meaningful.
findings.gap: No stated or measured expectation for availability or latency of document search and retrieval, so degradation is invisible and improvement cannot be prioritized by impact.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for the two critical journeys (search response and document retrieval), implement them as CloudWatch alarms on p95/p99 latency and error rate in IaC, and track an error budget.

findings.title: Business Metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics are emitted. There is no put_metric_data call or equivalent in index.cfm or download.cfm, and no dashboard definitions exist. Document searches, zero-result searches, and downloads are not measured.
findings.gap: Only default infrastructure metrics are available; there is no visibility into whether users are finding and retrieving documents successfully.
findings.recommendation: Emit custom CloudWatch metrics for searches performed, zero-result searches, and documents downloaded (with category dimensions), and publish them on a service dashboard alongside infrastructure metrics.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting
findings.description: No alerting is configured. The repository contains no CloudWatch alarms, anomaly detectors, composite alarms, or PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration — there is no IaC or configuration file in which such definitions could exist.
findings.gap: Failures of the single instance, the database, or the document disk generate no alert; detection depends on a user reporting the outage.
findings.recommendation: Start with static CloudWatch alarms on error rate, p99 latency, and service health, then layer CloudWatch anomaly detection on error rate and latency for the two critical paths, routed to on-call via SNS.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy
findings.description: README.md documents the deployment strategy as copying .cfm files over the network share to wwwroot on the single production instance. There is no CodeDeploy configuration, blue/green or canary setup, traffic shifting, health gate, or feature flags.
findings.gap: Every change goes directly to production on the only instance, with no staged rollout, verification step, or rollback path other than copying old files back.
findings.recommendation: Deploy through CodeDeploy (or ECS blue/green) with health checks and automated rollback, and shift traffic progressively via a load balancer or weighted target groups once the service runs on multiple instances.

findings.title: Integration Testing
findings.description: There are no automated tests of any kind. The repository contains four files (README.md, index.cfm, download.cfm, .gitignore) — no test directory, test files, test runner configuration, or CI pipeline to execute tests in.
findings.gap: No regression safety net exists for search or download behavior — the largest risk multiplier for the recommended database, storage, and runtime migrations, since correctness after cutover cannot be verified automatically.
findings.recommendation: Before any migration, write characterization/integration tests against the two endpoints (search returns expected documents for a known fixture; download returns expected content for a known doc_id; unauthenticated access is rejected) and run them in CI on every change.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation
findings.description: No runbooks exist in any form — no runbook markdown, SSM Automation documents, Lambda remediation, or self-healing configuration. README.md documents the failure modes (reboot equals downtime, disk loss equals data loss) but provides no response procedure.
findings.gap: Incident response for a documented single-point-of-failure system is entirely ad hoc, with no recovery procedure for the two known catastrophic scenarios.
findings.recommendation: Author versioned runbooks for instance loss, database loss, and document-disk loss; encode repeatable steps as SSM Automation documents; and automate recovery once backups and managed services are in place.

findings.title: Observability Ownership
findings.description: There are no observability assets to own and no ownership metadata: no dashboards, alarms, SLO files, CODEOWNERS, or team tags. README.md and the index.cfm header comments identify the application only as an ACME intranet portal last edited in 2016, with no named owner.
findings.gap: Monitoring is fragmented and reactive, and no team is accountable for the service's operational health or alert response.
findings.recommendation: Assign a named owning team, add CODEOWNERS covering the service and its observability definitions, and create a per-service dashboard and alarm set with owner tags and team-attributed SLOs.

evaluations.title: Workflow Orchestration
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — archetype-calibrated for data-gateway: no multi-step workflows exist in the read path and no background maintenance jobs were found. Dedicated orchestration is not applicable and is not a gap.

evaluations.title: Async Messaging and Streaming
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — archetype-calibrated for data-gateway: synchronous reads dominate and are the correct design; no write-back, cache-invalidation, or indexing flow requires messaging, and no self-managed broker is present.

evaluations.title: Async vs Sync Communication
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — archetype-calibrated for data-gateway: synchronous request/response is correct for both read endpoints; there are no inter-service calls at all. Converting to async is not recommended.

evaluations.title: Stored Procedures and Schema Complexity
evaluations.reason: Score 4 — no stored procedures, triggers, functions, .sql files, or proprietary T-SQL constructs found; both queries are plain SELECT statements and all logic is in the application layer.

evaluations.title: Audit Logging
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false — the repo contains no AWS-provisioning IaC and no account-level scope. CloudTrail is an account/organization-level service and belongs in the foundation infrastructure repo.

evaluations.title: Resource Tagging Governance
evaluations.reason: has_iac_provisioning_aws_resources=false — the repo provisions no AWS resources, so there is nothing to tag. Tagging governance belongs in the repo that owns the AWS infrastructure.

pathways.name: Move to Cloud Native
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: APP-Q2 < 3 (primary) AND at least one of INF-Q1 < 3, APP-Q3 < 3, APP-Q4 < 3

triggering_questions.note: Primary — tightly coupled CFML page monolith with no module or data boundaries
Supporting — all compute on a single raw Windows EC2 instance
Supporting — unbounded synchronous reads on the search and download paths

immediate_actions: Write characterization tests for the search and download endpoints before any extraction
Extract a document-search service and a document-retrieval service behind an Anti-corruption Layer over the existing documents schema
Move document storage behind a port so the local-disk adapter can be replaced by S3

pathways.name: Move to Containers
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q1 < 3 AND no container definitions found; guard not engaged because compute is a Windows EC2/IIS VM rather than Lambda/Fargate/ECS

triggering_questions.note: Primary — single Windows Server 2008 EC2 instance with IIS 7 and ColdFusion 8; no Dockerfile, compose file, or Kubernetes manifest in the repo

container_readiness_blockers: ColdFusion 8 is unsupported with no maintained container base image
Application state (documents) is on a local writable disk
Configuration and credentials live in CF Administrator outside the repository
Windows + IIS dependency constrains base-image choices
immediate_actions: Externalize configuration and credentials out of CF Administrator
Move documents to S3 so the workload becomes stateless
Re-platform onto a supported runtime (or Lucee on Linux if CFML must be retained), then containerize

pathways.name: Move to Open Source
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: DATA-Q4 < 3 AND commercial DB engines detected (compound — both required)

triggering_questions.note: DATA-Q4 = 4 — no stored procedures, triggers, or proprietary SQL constructs found; primary condition not met

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Commercial SQL Server 2005 was detected, but the compound trigger requires DATA-Q4 < 3 and no stored procedures or proprietary SQL exist. The engine-licensing consideration is addressed under Move to Managed Databases, where Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL is offered as the license-reduction target.

triggering_questions.note: Primary — self-managed SQL Server 2005 co-located on the application EC2 instance
Supporting — engine past EOL (April 2016) and no version pinning anywhere

immediate_actions: Inventory the documents schema and migrate to RDS for SQL Server (lift) or Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL (license reduction) via DMS
Enable Multi-AZ, automated backups with retention, and KMS encryption at cutover
Move the datasource credential into Secrets Manager with rotation
Replace inline unparameterized queries with parameterized queries in a data access layer during the cutover

pathways.name: Move to Managed Analytics
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q4 < 3 AND evidence of data processing workloads must exist

triggering_questions.note: INF-Q4 = 4 — synchronous reads are the correct design for a data-gateway; primary condition not met

pathways.not_triggered_reason: Contextual guard: no streaming, ETL, Glue, Airflow, or data-pipeline artifacts were found, and the detected archetype is data-gateway with sync-only reads. There are no data processing workloads to migrate.

pathways.name: Move to Modern DevOps
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: INF-Q10 < 3 OR INF-Q11 < 3 (primary); OPS-Q5 < 3 and OPS-Q6 < 3 strengthen

triggering_questions.note: Primary — 0% IaC coverage; no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, SAM, or Helm artifacts
Primary — deployment is a manual file copy to wwwroot; no pipeline definitions
Supporting — direct-to-production with no staged rollout or rollback
Supporting — no automated tests of any kind

immediate_actions: Codify the target infrastructure in CloudFormation or CDK before migrating anything
Add a build → test → deploy pipeline with automated rollback
Write characterization tests for the two read endpoints and gate the pipeline on them
Replace file-copy releases with CodeDeploy (or ECS blue/green) and health-gated traffic shifting

pathways.name: Move to AI
pathways.key_trigger_criteria: No AI/agent frameworks, no vector DB, no RAG, no agent eval framework — requires AI/agent/LLM intent evidenced in the repository
pathways.not_triggered_reason: No AI/agent intent evidenced in the repository (no AI-related signal terms in dependencies, source, configuration, IaC, or documentation). Primary trigger conditions were not evaluated.

approach_options.recommendation: Insufficient alone — fixes coupling but leaves the EOL ColdFusion 8 runtime, EOL SQL Server 2005, and local-disk storage in place.
Recommended — only two routes, so each can be cut over independently behind an Anti-corruption Layer while the legacy portal stays available.
Not recommended here — lift-and-containerize carries an unsupported runtime with critical CVEs into the new platform.

approach_options.effort: Very High in general; Low for this 55-line surface
approach_options.recommendation: Generally recommended against; acceptable only because the surface is this small, and only after characterization tests exist.

patterns: Saga (only if write paths are reintroduced)
Event Sourcing (optional, for document access audit history)

effort_factors.module_boundaries: APP-Q2 = 1 — none; SQL, auth, and HTML in the same files
effort_factors.data_coupling: DATA-Q2 = 1 — inline cfquery per page, no DAO
effort_factors.stored_procedures: DATA-Q4 = 4 — none found, materially lowering migration effort
effort_factors.communication_patterns: APP-Q3 = 4 — synchronous reads correct for the archetype, no async redesign needed
effort_factors.cicd_maturity: INF-Q11 = 1 — manual file copy, pipeline must be built first
effort_factors.test_coverage: OPS-Q6 = 1 — no automated tests; highest risk multiplier

decomposition_strategy.calibrated_estimate: Medium overall effort, dominated by the data/storage migration and pipeline build rather than application code volume.
